newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian church calls for moderation after violence.
newsitem.headline: Serbian church calls for moderation after violence.

text.p: The leader of the Serbian Orthodox Church called on Monday for moderation after a bloody crackdown by police on peaceful demonstrators overnight, and lashed out at President Slobodan Milosevic's government.

"Since the beginning of this misfortune, so unnecessary and dangerous for our country and people, I have sent a score of messages and pleas for peace and for a just and democratic settlement," Patriarch Pavle said.
"Last night's events forbode the worst," the 82-year old said in his message to the Serb people and the authorities, a copy of which was faxed to Reuters.
"I will not cease to plead and to beg the embittered people, the young and the old, to refrain from any provocation of unrest," he said.

The patriarch said he was appealing against violence "also to those who are armed as guardians of peace and order and not of the regime, which is so tragically for all of us sinking more and more into ignorance of what it is doing".
"I trust in God he will open its (the regime's) eyes and that it it will stop abusing the suffering people," he said.

The Church has joined a chorus of condemnation in Serbia and abroad against authorities who refuse to restore annulled opposition victories in 14 Serbian cities, including Belgrade, at local elections in November.
The patriarch himself led a 300,000-strong procession a week ago across Belgrade to break a police grip on the centre of the town.
The latest call comes after Milosevic's feared security police injured more than 100 people overnight in the worst political violence seen in Belgrade for years.
